subject: combination of predicted values in spatial-temporal model

messages.author: dab85ab569953d94
messages.subject: combination of predicted values in spatial-temporal model
parts:
Dear group, 

I am hoping to get some help on how to get the combination of the predicted values in spatial-temporal models. Below I created a reproducible example using data from Chapter 8.6 of Bayesian inference with INLA by Virgilio Gómez-Rubio.

I used the brainNM dataset which provides observed and expected counts of cases of brain cancer in the counties of New Mexico from 1973 to 1991. Now suppose that I would like to predict the county-level new cases for 1992 and I am able to do so using the code below. However, my question is that,  how do I get the predicted total cases for 1992 with associated posterior summaries (i.e., 0.025 and 0.975 qunatiles)? Conceptually this is pretty straightforward, as it will be summing over all county-level prediction for 1992. But how do I code it up? 

Thank you so much for your help!


###################
library("DClusterm")
data(brainNM)

nm.adj <- poly2nb(brainst@sp)
adj.mat <- as(nb2mat(nm.adj, style = "B"), "Matrix")

dat <- brainst@data
dat$id.time <- brainst@data$Year - 1973 + 1
dat$id.space <- as.numeric(dat$ID)
dat$id.spacetime <- 1:nrow(dat)

## Fitting a model
prec.prior <- list(prec = list(param = c(0.001, 0.001)))

brain.st <- inla(Observed ~ 1 + f(Year, model = "rw1", hyper = prec.prior) + 
        f(id.space, model = "besag", graph = adj.mat, hyper = prec.prior) +
                 f(id.spacetime, model="iid", hyper=prec.prior), 
                 data = dat, E = Expected, family = "poisson",
                 control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE, link = 1))

summary(brain.st)

### prediction
dat.tmp <- dat[dat$Year==1991, ]
dat.tmp$Observed  <- NA
dat.tmp$Expected <- 1

dat.pred <- rbind(dat, dat.tmp)
brain.st.pred <- inla(Observed ~ 1 + f(Year, model = "rw1", hyper = prec.prior) + 
                   f(id.space, model = "besag", graph = adj.mat, hyper = prec.prior) +
                   f(id.spacetime, model="iid", hyper=prec.prior), 
                 data = dat.pred, E = Expected, family = "poisson",
                 control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE, link = 1))
summary(brain.st.pred)
### extract prediction of individual county 
dat.pred$pred <- brain.st.pred$summary.fitted.values[, "mean"]
## how do I get the sum of the county of predicted values?

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] combination of predicted values in spatial-temporal model
parts:
Hi,

This depends a bit on whether you need total-count prediction, or if it’s enough to get sum-of-expectations prediction. In both cases, the general method is to use inla.posterior.sample(), from which you can compute/estimate the posterior distribution of any functional of the model. For count-prediction, you also need to add the data-level model simulation on top of the latent model simulation.

Some of this is made a bit easier in the inlabru package (github.com/inlabru-org/inlabru ). See the Articles on the github.io site linked from the README for examples from ecology. I think there’s an animal abundance estimation example there that even does something slightly more clever in the data-level step, by integrating the pdf:s instead of generating raw count samples.

Finn
